Reporting and prediction for paired affine-ratio results

Source: R/user-dnn-affine-ratio-methods.R
affine_ratio_result.Rd

These methods apply to affine_ratio_result and its clate_result subclass. Intervals are pointwise normal-reference intervals with frozen-score standard errors. A zero or numerically unavailable ratio variance gives NA interval bounds, not a zero-width confidence interval.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'affine_ratio_result'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'affine_ratio_result'
vcov(object, target = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'affine_ratio_result'
confint(object, parm = NULL, level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'affine_ratio_result'
summary(object, level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'affine_ratio_result'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.affine_ratio_result'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'affine_ratio_result'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  X0 = NULL,
  x0 = NULL,
  se.fit = FALSE,
  interval = c("none", "confidence"),
  level = 0.95,
  ...
)

Arguments

object, x

A fitted affine_ratio_result or clate_result.

...

Not used.

target

Optional single target index for vcov.

parm

Optional numeric target indices for confint.

level

Confidence level in (0,1).

digits

Printing precision.

newdata

Optional reporting-target matrix/data frame. For a data-frame fit, only the retained reporting columns are extracted.

X0, x0

Target matrix or single target vector, alternatives to newdata.

se.fit

Whether prediction returns standard errors.

interval

Either "none" or "confidence".

Value

coef returns a named vector; vcov returns one marginal matrix or a list of marginal matrices; confint returns a two-column matrix. summary returns a classed list with coefficients, level, has_se and meta, plus component and per-target status tables. The coefficient table follows the CATE estimate/std.error/statistic/p.value/conf.low/conf.high schema. predict returns a vector, a fit/se.fit list or a fit/lwr/upr matrix. Printing returns its input invisibly.

Details

Covariance matrices are on the estimator scale. Prediction changes reporting targets only, holding the observations, signals and order fixed. It never trains nuisance models. A supplied-training label does not verify the statistical or causal assumptions underlying inference.

Examples

f <- affine_ratio_dnn(
  X = matrix(1:4, ncol = 1), x0 = 0,
  numerator = c(2, 1, 4, 3), denominator = c(1, -1, 2, 1), s = 2
)
coef(f)
#> target_1 
#>        4 
vcov(f)
#>       theta
#> theta    34
confint(f)
#>           conf.low conf.high
#> target_1 -7.428456  15.42846
summary(f)
#>   localization: s = 2, s/n = 0.5
#> Components: numerator = numerator; denominator = denominator
#> Ratio statuses: ok=1
#>          estimate std.error statistic p.value conf.low conf.high
#> target_1        4     5.831     0.686  0.4927   -7.428     15.43
predict(f, x0 = 5, se.fit = TRUE)
#> $fit
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $se.fit
#> [1] 1.414214
#>
